item.title: How To Not Be The Ashley Tisdale In Your Friend Group
item.description: When Ashley Tisdale wrote a viral essay about stepping away from what she described as a “toxic” mom group, the reaction was swift and deeply divided.

item.title: Womanhood Was Never Meant To Be Cured
item.description: From puberty to menopause, nearly every phase of being a woman is now framed as a problem in need of expert intervention.

item.title: The Valentine's Lingerie He Hopes You'll Wear: 5 Pieces Worth Buying
item.description: What your hubby really wants you to buy this Valentine's Day, according to data, surveys, and a little hands-on experimentation.

item.title: Are You Being Honest Or Just Rude? How To Tell The Difference
item.description: In a culture that values being “real,” speaking plainly is often framed as a moral good, regardless of timing, tone, or consequence.

item.title: Deadbeat Dads Are A Feminist Side Effect
item.description: There’s nothing less masculine than a deadbeat dad. But this discouraging modern archetype is not a product of the patriarchy, quite the opposite actually.

item.title: Frosted 2000s Lips Are Back: How To Get The Look
item.description: People are feeling nostalgic. Many of us are yearning for the wholesome, analog years of our youth, when conversations were clear of smartphone interruptions and tables were dressed with unprocessed foods.

item.title: How Calling Women “Pick Mes” Became A Tool Of Ideological Enforcement
item.description: Who better to compose a dossier on what a “pick me” is than Evie Magazine? We’re regularly touted as “conservative Cosmo for pick mes,” after all, but what even is a pick me, and is it ever a valid assertion?

item.title: How To Stop Apologizing For Your Life
item.description: Somewhere along the way, women learned to apologize for their lives before anyone even asked them to.

item.title: If "People We Meet on Vacation" Made You Emotional, This Is Why
item.description: If "People We Meet on Vacation" left you with that quiet, aching feeling you couldn’t quite name, it’s because the film isn’t really about love or travel, but about the versions of ourselves we grieve without realizing it.

item.title: The Truth About The Honeymoon Phase No One Prepares You For
item.description: We’re told that the beginning of love should be light, easy, and intoxicating. A period of magical romance where chemistry carries everything forward and doubt has no place. And if it doesn’t feel that way, something must be “wrong.”
